newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 to build on upturn on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 to build on upturn on Wall Street.

text.p: A late swing into positive territory on Wall Street raised Belgian investor hopes that the Brussels' Bel-20 share index would build on Wednesday's 0.78 percent gain, dealers said.

The index rose by 18.40 points to end at 2,373.59 on the back of firmer bonds, benign German inflation data and Tuesday's two percent gain on Wall Street. Buying of selected stocks, notably retailers and other cyclicals, also helped.
One trader said the market was now on track again to re-visit 2,400 points on the Bel-20. Further out, his target was 2,500. "The market likes round numbers, psychologically."

He said the bourse was underpinned by the view that economic fundamentals remained sound -- interest rates and inflation were low and no major changes were expected; growth was forecast to pick up, bolstering the outlook for company profits.
But another advised caution, saying that his target for the year had been 2,300 points and that he did not see much scope for a rise above that.

"It has all gone a bit quickly...(also) Wall Street remains dangerous," he said. In Monday's session the Dow Jones lost some 2.5 percent, recouping that loss again on Tuesday, but the wide swings had made him nervous.
"We believe in the bourse in the longer run, but for now it is better to hold back some cash (for stock picking)," he said.
